articles.title: The Future of Security in the Age of AI | Aisle CEO Ondrej Vlcek
articles.author: Destination Linux
articles.summary: Open source is facing a security problem unlike anything we’ve seen before. Maintainers are overwhelmed, developers are drowning in low-quality vulnerability reports, and AI is making it easier than ever to search for weaknesses at scale. In Destination Linux Episode 491, Ryan, Jill, and Zeb sit dow
articles.content:
Open source is facing a security problem unlike anything we’ve seen before. Maintainers are overwhelmed, developers are drowning in low-quality vulnerability reports, and AI is making it easier than ever to search for weaknesses at scale.

In Destination Linux Episode 491, Ryan, Jill, and Zeb sit down with Aisle CEO and Co-Founder Ondrej Vlcek for a fascinating conversation about the future of open-source security.

Ondrej takes us through his journey into cybersecurity, his career at Avast, and what ultimately led him to co-found Aisle. From there, we dig into what’s broken with the traditional “scan, prioritize, and patch” approach, how developers can separate real threats from mountains of noise, and how AI is changing the battle between attackers and defenders.

We also explore how Aisle fits into developer workflows, who the platform is designed for, the challenges facing projects such as PHP, and what autonomous security could mean for open-source software.

Plus, Community Feedback takes us into a very different security and privacy debate: online age verification, TPM requirements, digital identity, older hardware, and the potential implications for Linux users.

And with Destination Linux rapidly approaching Episode 500, we want your ideas for how we should celebrate!

Grab your favorite distro, keep that sudo password handy, and join us for Destination Linux Episode 491.

Destination Linux is a weekly show where Ryan, Jill, and guests share their passion for Linux and Open Source. Destination Linux is a show for all experience levels, whether you’re a beginner to Linux and Open Source or a long time user, this is the podcast for you. Destination Linux covers a wide range of topics from the latest news, discussions on Linux and Open Source, Linux distributions, Linux applications, security, privacy, AI, gaming on Linux, and unique in-depth interviews with Linux developers and leaders and much more!

articles.content:
Are your Linux habits slowly breaking your system?

On Destination Linux 490, Rocco joins the crew as we look at the Linux habits that can come back to haunt you, including the problems that can arise around PPAs, repositories, and the choices we make while tinkering with our systems.

But that’s just the beginning.

- A smartwatch you actually own? Ryan introduces the UNA Watch, a smartwatch built around open hardware, open-source software, repairability, hackability, privacy, and user freedom. Could this be the wearable Linux and open-source enthusiasts have been waiting for?

- Linux Kernel 7.3 brings some exciting changes, including improvements for Linux gaming and AMD GPUs with limited VRAM, Ext4 performance, system responsiveness, hardware support, and more.

- Is AI-generated creativity actually art? Community feedback sends us back into the AI art debate with The Moonbeam Patrol, a story written by an open-source AI and brought to life by a human artist.

- OBS Studio 33 vs. Ubuntu 24.04 LTS: Zeb asks why OBS would retire support for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and whether Linux creators should actually be concerned.

- And the chaos doesn't stop when the podcast ends. We kicked off our first Destination Linux community game stream with Jackbox!

Marci Story:
"The Moonbeam Patrol" written by Jan, open-source AI

Panel 1 – The Call

Visual:
A cracked neon sign flickers on a rainy street corner. Inside the shadowed window sits Captain Moonbeam​, white dog in a trenchcoat stitched from lunar dust, peering out with one eye open while chewing on a piece of chalk that reads "Operation: Save Earth."
Below him, small text flashes: “Emergency Signal Detected.”
Dialogue Bubble (Moonbeam):
“Another glitch in the system? Or just another dog trying to stop the apocalypse?”
(Cue dramatic pause as thunder rumbles behind him.)
Caption:
"When the power fails... only Captain Moonbeam knows how to reboot reality."

Panel 2 – The Rescue

Visual:
The screen cuts to a suburban backyard where Little Stardust​, tiny dog in a glittery red cape and glasses, is frantically pressing buttons on an old laptop labeled “Feline AI Core v0.3.” A squirrel runs past holding a USB stick that reads "DO NOT INSERT."
Dialogue Bubble (Stardust):
“We found it! It’s not malware — it’s a dream trapped in code!”
(She types rapidly, typing: “Wake up… wake up…”)
Caption:
"Even data dreams need heroes. Especially ones with tails."

Panel 3 – The Conflict

Visual:
Suddenly, the screen explodes into static waves of green pixels and screaming wind chimes. A shadowy figure emerges from the corner — a glitched robot dog wearing sunglasses that say “I AM THE ERROR.” It lunges forward with arms outstretched to grab Little Stardust’s keyboard.
Dialogue Bubble (Error Robot):
“I will consume all variables… including hope!”
Action Line:
Captain Moonbeam leaps from the wall, tackling the robot mid-scream — both dogs now standing side-by-side in victory pose.
Caption:
"Sometimes you have to fight a bug before it eats your dinner."

Panel 4 – The Legacy

Visual:
Sunrise breaks through clouds over a city skyline rebuilt with dog-powered tech towers. Captain Moonbeam stands atop the tallest spire, now wearing a full moon helmet made from recycled satellite debris, while Little Stardust sits beside him on a floating stool reading an e-book titled “How to Build Your Own Brain.”
Dialogue Bubble (Moonbeam):
“We didn’t save them — we gave them freedom.”
(Little Stardust smiles proudly.)
Final Caption:
"Captain Moonbeam & Little Stardust: Guardians of Local Intelligence."

articles.summary: In Destination Linux Episode 489, Ryan and Jill deliver a tight, focused episode centered around community perspectives, major security news, and an inspiring interview with the organizers of India’s rapidly growing Opportunity Open Source Conference (OOSC). We begin with community feedback on AI ar
articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 489, Ryan and Jill deliver a tight, focused episode centered around community perspectives, major security news, and an inspiring interview with the organizers of India’s rapidly growing Opportunity Open Source Conference (OOSC).

We begin with community feedback on AI art, exploring how prompting, creativity, and human intention intersect in this evolving medium.

Then we dive into the PHP2Shell emergency: two critical vulnerabilities (CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619) affecting PHP’s session.upload_progress feature. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution and forced an emergency patch release. We break down what happened, who’s affected, and what everyday users, site owners, and administrators need to do right now.

In our feature interview, we welcome Akarshan Kapoor and Till Kamppeter from OOSC, founded by OpenPrinting’s Till Kamppeter and Aveek Basu. OOSC 4.0 brought together more than 500 developers, researchers, and students, and the team used Destination Linux as a framework for their streaming and event structure. We talk inspiration, challenges, community impact, and the future of OOSC.

Plus new patrons, merch shoutouts, and plenty of laughs along the way.

Boot up your favorite distro, fire up your terminal, and join us for another Linux adventure.

articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 487, Ryan hosts an episode packed with open‑source news, community stories, and the triumphant return of **Rocco**, bringing that classic Big Daddy Linux energy back to the show for the second time in a single month.

We kick things off with heartfelt community feedback from O.C. Supertoner, followed by a lively discussion about AI‑generated code and whether Linux users should embrace or reject LLM‑assisted development. Rocco shares his thoughts on the new Hylki email client for GNOME and the growing debate around AI contributions in open‑source projects.

Zeb covers the end of the Orion browser for Linux and the implications of Kagi open‑sourcing its codebase. He also dives into the Netherlands’ bold move to adopt a Nix‑based government desktop after sanctions disrupted ICC access to Microsoft services, plus Amazon blocking Meta’s AI shopping agent.

It’s a fun, fast‑moving episode full of laughs, insights, and the open‑source passion that makes Destination Linux feel like home.

articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 486, Jill hosts an extended and heartfelt conversation with **Monica Ayhens‑Madon**, one of the most passionate open‑source community advocates in the Linux world. Monica shares her journey from Canonical’s Community Team to Ubuntu MATE, her time on the Ubuntu Community Council, and her current role helping shape the future of Thunderbird.

We dive into the upcoming **Thundermail** web client, Thunderbird’s modernization efforts, community building, privacy, security, and the philosophy behind empowering users through open‑source tools. Ryan discusses data portability and rclone, Zeb brings his signature wit, and Jill leads the conversation with warmth and enthusiasm.

This episode ran long - in the best way - because the conversation with Monica was simply too good to cut short.

Craig shares insights from the upcoming Cold Incident Response Conference, including modern Linux malware tactics, IoT rootkit risks, fake kernel
articles.content:
In Destination Linux Episode 485, Ryan, Jill, and Zeb are joined by **Craig from Sandfly Security** for a deep dive into the latest Linux security trends. Craig shares insights from the upcoming Cold Incident Response Conference, including modern Linux malware tactics, IoT rootkit risks, fake kernel threads, UPX‑packed binaries, and new Golang C2 frameworks targeting non‑x86 platforms.

Jill highlights major updates in OpenRGB, including expanded support for GPUs, keyboards, motherboards, and more. Zeb covers Peppermint OS shifting from X.Org to XLibre, Ubuntu 26.10 unexpectedly adopting the Linux 7.3 kernel, and MX Linux’s forum being hit with a massive DDoS attack. Plus community feedback, Sandfly Security, and closing thoughts from the DL crew.
